grades.label: Reliability
grades.question: Will it still be here, and still be open, if a key person leaves?

signals.label: Bus factor
signals.measure: Fewest people who wrote half of the last year's human commits
signals.why: When one person writes most of the code, the project stalls if they step away. The top contributor's share was one of the strongest predictors of whether a project stayed maintained.

signals.label: Active contributors
signals.measure: People (not bots) with a commit in the last 12 months
signals.why: With more people involved, fixes keep coming when someone gets busy.

signals.label: Backing
signals.measure: Owner is a foundation or nonprofit (1), an organization (0.6), or a personal account (0.3)
signals.why: In one study, 63% of projects that became unmaintained belonged to personal accounts, while 74% of active ones belonged to organizations. We verify foundation status by hand.

signals.label: License
signals.measure: OSI and FSF approved (1), one of the two (0.9), unrecognized (0.5), source-available (0.25), none (0)
signals.why: An open license lets anyone keep the code alive if the original team walks away. A repo being public doesn't make it open.

signals.label: Age
signals.measure: Years since the first commit (full credit at 5)
signals.why: A project that has lasted years has survived real use.

signals.label: Track record
signals.why: A deep history shows sustained work. Past 2,000 commits, more adds little.

grades.label: Maintenance
grades.question: Is someone actively fixing, releasing, and documenting it?

signals.label: Recent activity
signals.measure: Human commits in the last 90 days (full credit at 50)
signals.why: Commits in the most recent three months were the strongest single predictor of whether a project is maintained.

signals.label: Steadiness
signals.measure: Longest stretch without commits in the last 12 months (0 days earns full credit, 180 or more earns none)
signals.why: Long silences were the next-strongest warning sign.

signals.label: Follow-through
signals.measure: Issues and pull requests closed, divided by those opened, over the last 12 months
signals.why: Shows whether bug reports and contributions get answered.

signals.label: Release freshness
signals.measure: Days since the latest release (half credit after one year)
signals.why: This is gentle on purpose. A quiet year can mean a project is finished, not abandoned.

signals.label: Release cadence
signals.measure: Releases in the last 12 months (full credit at 6)
signals.why: Public releases give people a stable version to install.

signals.label: Documentation
signals.measure: README (1/3), plus a docs site or folder (1/3), plus docs edited in the last year (1/3)
signals.why: If nobody can learn how to use it, nobody can help maintain it.

grades.label: Security
grades.question: Does it follow security practices you can see from outside?

signals.label: Release integrity
signals.measure: Signatures (1) or checksums (0.5) published with the latest release
signals.why: Lets you confirm a download wasn't tampered with. This weight matches OpenSSF Scorecard's High-risk Signed-Releases check.

signals.label: Dependency updates
signals.measure: Dependabot or Renovate is configured to keep dependencies patched
signals.why: Most security holes arrive through outdated dependencies. Scorecard rates this check High risk.

signals.label: Code review
signals.measure: Share of the last 20 merged changes that someone other than the author approved or merged
signals.why: A second pair of eyes catches mistakes and sabotage. Scorecard rates this check High risk. It runs only in our weekly job, not in live checks.

signals.label: Security policy
signals.measure: A SECURITY file explains how to report a vulnerability privately
signals.why: Gives people a safe way to report problems before attackers find them. Scorecard rates this check Medium risk.

signals.label: Automated tests
signals.measure: CI workflows run automatically on changes
signals.why: Catches breakage before release. Scorecard rates this check Low risk.

signals.label: Best-practices badge
signals.measure: OpenSSF Best Practices badge: passing (0.5), silver or gold (1)
signals.why: A self-certified checklist reviewed by OpenSSF. Scorecard rates this check Low risk.
